In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PD‐L1 is a biomarker that enriches for responses to PD‐L1 or PD‐1 inhibitors, and that the absence of PD‐L1 does not exclude the potential for clinical benefit.
PD‐L1 is a predictive marker in NSCLC that is not perfect.
PD‐L1 is a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in NSCLC, but it is not the only predictive biomarker and it should not be used in isolation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PD‐L1 biomarker is not ready for prime time, but it is not ready to be discarded either.
PD‐L1 positivity in a single tumor biopsy is not sufficient to predict response, and PD‐L1 negativity in a single biopsy is not sufficient for exclusion.
PD‐L1 heterogeneity is a real phenomenon, which can be observed at the intertumoral, intratumoral, and interassay levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of PD‐L1 to select patients for PD‐1 or PD‐L 1 inhibitors should be based on the clinical trial data and not on the level of positivity or heterogeneity.
PD‐L1 positivity is not a binary event.

the use of a single‐biopsy, single‐tumor PD‐L1 assay may not accurately identify patients who will respond to PD‐1/PD‐L1 inhibitors, and that the lack of PD‐L1‐positive tumors does not exclude clinical activity.
